question_en: The Battle of Plassey (1757) was fought between the British East India Company and the Nawab of Bengal, who was:
explanation_en: Robert Clive defeated Siraj-ud-Daulah on 23 June 1757, helped by the treachery of Mir Jafar.

question_en: The Company obtained the Diwani (revenue collection rights) of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa in 1765 through the Treaty of Allahabad from:
explanation_en: After winning Buxar (1764), Clive secured the Diwani from the Mughal emperor Shah Alam II.

question_en: Which was the first Indian state to accept Lord Wellesley's Subsidiary Alliance (1798)?
explanation_en: The Nizam of Hyderabad was the first to sign the Subsidiary Alliance in 1798; Awadh followed in 1801.

question_en: The first princely state annexed by the British under Lord Dalhousie's Doctrine of Lapse was:
explanation_en: Satara was annexed in 1848; Jhansi (1853) and Nagpur (1854) followed.

question_en: The Revolt of 1857 began on 10 May 1857 at:
explanation_en: Sepoys at Meerut rebelled and marched to Delhi, proclaiming Bahadur Shah Zafar as their leader.

question_en: Who was the first Viceroy of India after the Government of India Act, 1858 transferred power to the Crown?
explanation_en: Canning, the last Governor-General, became the first Viceroy in 1858.

question_en: The Partition of Bengal (1905), announced by Lord Curzon, was annulled in 1911 during the viceroyalty of:
explanation_en: At the 1911 Delhi Durbar King George V annulled the partition and shifted the capital from Calcutta to Delhi; Hardinge was Viceroy.

question_en: The Indian National Congress was founded in 1885; who was its first president?
explanation_en: A. O. Hume helped found it, but the first session at Bombay was presided over by W. C. Bonnerjee.

question_en: Which committee was appointed to inquire into the Jallianwala Bagh massacre of 13 April 1919?
explanation_en: The Hunter Committee (1919-20) investigated the Punjab disturbances and General Dyer's firing at Amritsar.

question_en: Gandhiji suspended the Non-Cooperation Movement in February 1922 after the violent incident at:
explanation_en: A mob burned a police station at Chauri Chaura (UP) on 5 February 1922, killing policemen, so Gandhi called the movement off.

question_en: Gandhiji began the Dandi March (Salt Satyagraha) on 12 March 1930 from:
explanation_en: He walked about 385 km with 78 followers and broke the salt law at Dandi on 6 April 1930.

question_en: The Poona Pact (1932) was signed between Gandhiji and Dr B. R. Ambedkar after the announcement of the:
explanation_en: Gandhi's fast against separate electorates for the Depressed Classes ended with the Poona Pact, which gave them reserved seats in joint electorates.

question_en: The Quit India resolution was passed in August 1942 at which venue in Bombay?
explanation_en: The AICC passed the resolution on 8 August 1942 at Gowalia Tank Maidan (now August Kranti Maidan) and Gandhi gave the call 'Do or Die'.

question_en: Which of the following was a member of the Cabinet Mission that came to India in 1946?
explanation_en: The Mission comprised Pethick-Lawrence, Stafford Cripps and A. V. Alexander; Wavell was the Viceroy and Attlee the Prime Minister.

question_en: The words 'Socialist', 'Secular' and 'Integrity' were added to the Preamble by which Constitutional Amendment?
explanation_en: The 42nd Amendment is the only one to have changed the Preamble.

question_en: Who was the Chairman of the Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly?
explanation_en: Ambedkar chaired the seven-member Drafting Committee; Rajendra Prasad was President of the Assembly and B. N. Rau its constitutional adviser.

question_en: The Constituent Assembly took how much time to complete the framing of the Constitution?
explanation_en: The Assembly met first on 9 December 1946 and adopted the Constitution on 26 November 1949.

question_en: Which Article guarantees 'equality before the law and equal protection of the laws'?
explanation_en: Article 14 applies to all persons; Articles 15 and 16 deal with non-discrimination and equal opportunity in public employment.

question_en: The Right to Education for children aged 6 to 14 years became a Fundamental Right under Article 21A through which amendment?
explanation_en: The 86th Amendment inserted Article 21A; the RTE Act, 2009 gave it effect from 1 April 2010.

question_en: Dr Ambedkar called which Article the 'heart and soul' of the Constitution?
explanation_en: Article 32 gives the right to approach the Supreme Court for enforcement of Fundamental Rights.

question_en: How many Fundamental Duties are listed in Article 51A at present?
explanation_en: Ten duties were added by the 42nd Amendment (1976) and the 11th (duty of parents to educate children aged 6-14) by the 86th Amendment (2002).

question_en: The Directive Principles of State Policy are contained in which Part of the Constitution?
explanation_en: Part IV (Articles 36 to 51) holds the DPSPs, which are non-justiciable and borrowed from the Irish Constitution.

question_en: Which Article of the Constitution directs the State to organise village panchayats?
explanation_en: Article 40 is a Directive Principle; Panchayati Raj was later given constitutional status by the 73rd Amendment.

question_en: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act added which Schedule listing 29 subjects for Panchayats?
explanation_en: The 73rd Amendment inserted Part IX and the Eleventh Schedule; the 74th added the Twelfth Schedule (18 subjects) for municipalities.

question_en: What is the maximum strength of the Rajya Sabha as per the Constitution?
explanation_en: Up to 238 members represent States and UTs and 12 are nominated by the President, making 250.

question_en: Which Constitutional Amendment is popularly called the 'Mini-Constitution' because of the wide changes it made?
explanation_en: The 42nd Amendment, passed during the Emergency, altered the Preamble, added Fundamental Duties and curbed judicial review.

question_en: The 44th Constitutional Amendment (1978) removed which right from the list of Fundamental Rights?
explanation_en: Article 31 was deleted; property became a legal right under Article 300A in Part XII.

question_en: The minimum voting age was reduced from 21 to 18 years by which Constitutional Amendment?
explanation_en: The 61st Amendment amended Article 326; the change took effect in 1989.

question_en: The Goods and Services Tax (GST) was introduced through which Constitutional Amendment Act?
explanation_en: The 101st Amendment inserted Article 279A (GST Council); GST was rolled out on 1 July 2017.

question_en: The 103rd Constitutional Amendment Act (2019) provided reservation of how much for Economically Weaker Sections in general category?
explanation_en: It added Articles 15(6) and 16(6) for EWS reservation in education and public employment, upheld by the Supreme Court in 2022.

question_en: The Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam (106th Amendment, 2023) provides what reservation for women in the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies?
explanation_en: It reserves one-third of seats, including within SC/ST quotas, but will be applied only after the next Census and delimitation.

question_en: Under which Article can the President be removed from office by impeachment?
explanation_en: Article 61 sets the procedure: a charge of 'violation of the Constitution' needs a two-thirds majority in both Houses.

question_en: The anti-defection law was added to the Constitution through the Tenth Schedule by which amendment?
explanation_en: The 52nd Amendment added the Tenth Schedule; the 91st (2003) tightened it by banning splits and capping ministers at 15 per cent.

question_en: The 'basic structure' doctrine, limiting Parliament's power to amend the Constitution, was laid down in:

options.en: Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India (1978)
Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala (1973)
A. K. Gopalan v. State of Madras (1950)

explanation_en: A 13-judge bench ruled 7:6 that Parliament can amend but cannot destroy the basic structure; Golaknath had denied any power to amend Part III.

question_en: The writ of Habeas Corpus literally means:
explanation_en: The writ is issued to produce a detained person before the court to test legality of detention; 'Mandamus' means 'we command'.

question_en: A Money Bill passed by the Lok Sabha must be returned by the Rajya Sabha, with or without recommendations, within:
explanation_en: Under Article 109, if the Rajya Sabha does not return it within 14 days it is deemed passed; the Lok Sabha may reject its recommendations.

question_en: Who presides over a joint sitting of both Houses of Parliament called under Article 108?
explanation_en: The Speaker presides; in absence the Deputy Speaker, then the Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.

question_en: President's Rule in a State, on failure of constitutional machinery, is imposed under which Article?
explanation_en: Article 352 deals with National Emergency and Article 360 with Financial Emergency.

question_en: Under Article 249, Parliament can legislate on a State List subject in the national interest if which House passes a resolution by a two-thirds majority?
explanation_en: The Rajya Sabha, as the House of the States, must declare by two-thirds of members present and voting that it is expedient in national interest.

question_en: Which is the longest river of peninsular India?
explanation_en: The Godavari (about 1,465 km) is the longest peninsular river and is called 'Dakshin Ganga'.

question_en: The river Yamuna, flowing through Delhi, originates from:
explanation_en: It rises from the Yamunotri glacier on the Bandarpoonch range in Uttarakhand and joins the Ganga at Prayagraj.

question_en: The highest mountain peak located entirely within India is:
explanation_en: Kangchenjunga (8,586 m, Sikkim) is the third highest in the world; K2 lies in Gilgit-Baltistan and Everest in Nepal-Tibet.

question_en: The highest peak of the Western Ghats and of peninsular India is:
explanation_en: Anamudi (2,695 m) is in the Anamalai hills of Kerala; Doddabetta (2,637 m) is the highest in the Nilgiris.

question_en: Black soil (regur), best suited for cotton cultivation, is mainly formed from the weathering of:
explanation_en: The Deccan Trap's basaltic lava gives black soil, which is rich in lime, iron and potash and retains moisture well.

question_en: The Tropic of Cancer passes through all of the following states EXCEPT:
explanation_en: It crosses eight states: Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura and Mizoram.

question_en: Which Indian state has the longest coastline on the mainland?
explanation_en: Gujarat has India's longest coastline (about 1,600 km), followed by Andhra Pradesh.

question_en: The south-west monsoon normally sets in over the Indian mainland first on the coast of:
explanation_en: The monsoon normally arrives at Kerala around 1 June and covers the whole country by about 8 July.

question_en: Chilika Lake, the largest coastal lagoon of India, is located in:
explanation_en: Chilika is a brackish water lagoon on the Odisha coast and a Ramsar site; Pulicat Lake lies on the Andhra Pradesh-Tamil Nadu border.

question_en: The winter rainfall in north-western India, useful for the rabi wheat crop, is caused by:

options.en: Cyclonic depressions of the Bay of Bengal

explanation_en: Western disturbances are extra-tropical storms that originate in the Mediterranean region and bring winter rain to Punjab, Haryana and Delhi.

question_en: Which of the following rivers flows westward into the Arabian Sea through a rift valley?
explanation_en: The Narmada flows west through a rift valley between the Vindhyas and Satpura and drains into the Gulf of Khambhat.

question_en: The Standard Meridian of India (82°30' E), on which Indian Standard Time is based, passes near which city?
explanation_en: IST is GMT+5:30; the 82°30' E meridian passes through Mirzapur in Uttar Pradesh.

question_en: The Andaman Islands are separated from the Nicobar Islands by the:
explanation_en: The Ten Degree Channel lies along 10° N; the Eight and Nine Degree Channels are in the Lakshadweep area, and Palk Strait separates India from Sri Lanka.

question_en: The Sundarbans, the largest mangrove forest of the world, is mainly the delta of which two rivers?
explanation_en: The Sundarbans delta in West Bengal and Bangladesh is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and home to the Royal Bengal Tiger.

question_en: The Jharia coalfield, the largest source of coking coal in India, is in:
explanation_en: Jharia, near Dhanbad, contains the best coking coal needed for steel making.

question_en: The Luni river, which rises in the Aravallis near Ajmer, ends in:
explanation_en: The Luni is an inland drainage river of Rajasthan that disappears in the marshes of the Rann of Kutch in Gujarat.

question_en: The repo rate is the rate at which:

options.en: The RBI lends short-term funds to commercial banks
Commercial banks lend to the public
The RBI borrows from commercial banks
Banks pay interest on savings deposits

explanation_en: Repo means repurchase agreement; reverse repo is the rate at which the RBI absorbs money from banks.

question_en: The Reserve Bank of India was nationalised in the year:
explanation_en: The RBI began on 1 April 1935 as a private shareholders' bank and was nationalised on 1 January 1949; 14 commercial banks were nationalised in 1969.

question_en: Fiscal deficit of the Government is equal to total expenditure minus:
explanation_en: Fiscal deficit shows the government's total borrowing requirement; primary deficit is fiscal deficit minus interest payments.

question_en: Which of the following is a tertiary sector activity?
explanation_en: Tertiary (service) sector includes banking, transport and education; farming and mining are primary and manufacturing is secondary.

question_en: The NITI Aayog replaced the Planning Commission on:
explanation_en: NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India) is a think tank chaired by the Prime Minister.

question_en: The Second Five Year Plan (1956-61) emphasised rapid industrialisation based on the model of:
explanation_en: The Second Plan stressed heavy industry and public sector expansion; the First Plan (1951-56) followed the Harrod-Domar model.

question_en: The GST Council, set up under Article 279A, is headed by:
explanation_en: The Union Finance Minister chairs it and State finance ministers are members; decisions need a three-fourths weighted majority.

question_en: Under the flexible inflation targeting framework adopted in 2016, the RBI targets which inflation measure at 4 per cent (with a band of plus or minus 2 per cent)?
explanation_en: The Monetary Policy Committee works with a CPI-based target of 4 per cent, tolerance band 2 to 6 per cent.

question_en: The Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) is the share of a bank's deposits that must be kept:

options.en: In government securities with the bank
As gold in its own vaults

explanation_en: CRR is held with the RBI and earns no interest; SLR is held by banks themselves in liquid assets such as G-secs and gold.

question_en: The 'Annual Financial Statement', commonly called the Union Budget, is presented to Parliament under which Article?
explanation_en: Article 112 requires the statement of estimated receipts and expenditure each year; Article 110 defines Money Bills and Article 280 the Finance Commission.

question_en: The chemical name of baking soda is:
explanation_en: Baking soda is NaHCO3; washing soda is Na2CO3.10H2O.

question_en: Which metal is stored under kerosene oil because it reacts vigorously with air and water?
explanation_en: Sodium and potassium are highly reactive, so they are kept immersed in kerosene to avoid fire.

question_en: Rusting of iron requires the presence of:
explanation_en: Rust is hydrated iron(III) oxide formed when iron is exposed to moist air; galvanisation prevents it.

question_en: The general formula of the homologous series of alkynes is:
explanation_en: Alkanes are CnH2n+2, alkenes CnH2n and alkynes CnH2n-2 (for example, ethyne C2H2).

question_en: Which allotrope of carbon is a good conductor of electricity?
explanation_en: Each carbon in graphite uses three bonds, leaving a free electron per atom, whereas diamond has all four electrons bonded.

question_en: Plaster of Paris is obtained by heating gypsum at 373 K. Its chemical formula is:
explanation_en: Gypsum is CaSO4.2H2O and loses 1.5 water molecules on heating; CaOCl2 is bleaching powder.

question_en: In the human digestive system, absorption of digested food mainly takes place in the:
explanation_en: The small intestine has finger-like villi that give a large surface area for absorption.

question_en: Salivary amylase present in saliva helps in the digestion of:
explanation_en: Salivary amylase breaks starch into maltose; pepsin acts on proteins and lipase on fats.

question_en: In a dihybrid cross between two pure parents with two contrasting traits, the phenotypic ratio in the F2 generation is:
explanation_en: Mendel's dihybrid cross of round-yellow and wrinkled-green seeds gave 9:3:3:1; a monohybrid cross gives 3:1.

question_en: According to the 10 per cent law, the energy that passes from one trophic level to the next is about:
explanation_en: Only about 10 per cent of energy is stored at the next level; the rest is lost as heat in respiration.

question_en: Myopia (short-sightedness) is corrected by using a lens that is:
explanation_en: In myopia the image forms in front of the retina; a concave lens diverges rays so that it falls on the retina. Hypermetropia needs a convex lens.

question_en: The power of a convex lens of focal length 50 cm is:
explanation_en: P = 1/f in metres = 1/0.5 = +2 D; a convex lens has positive power.

question_en: Two resistors of 6 ohm and 3 ohm are connected in parallel. Their equivalent resistance is:
explanation_en: 1/R = 1/6 + 1/3 = 3/6, so R = 2 ohm; series would give 9 ohm.

question_en: An electric generator works on the principle of:
explanation_en: Rotating a coil in a magnetic field changes the flux and induces current, a discovery of Faraday.

question_en: Which two architects are mainly associated with the design of New Delhi, inaugurated in 1931?

options.en: Charles Correa and B. V. Doshi
Robert T. Russell and Walter Sykes George

explanation_en: The capital's shift from Calcutta was announced at the 1911 Durbar; Lutyens and Baker designed Rashtrapati Bhavan and the Secretariat.

question_en: Which of the following is NOT a UNESCO World Heritage Site in Delhi?
explanation_en: Delhi has three World Heritage Sites; the Jantar Mantar World Heritage Site is the one in Jaipur.

question_en: Humayun's Tomb in Delhi, the first garden tomb on the Indian subcontinent, was commissioned by:
explanation_en: Humayun's widow Hamida Banu Begum had it built from 1565; it inspired the Taj Mahal's design.

question_en: The Jantar Mantar observatory in Delhi was built in 1724 by:
explanation_en: Jai Singh II of Amber built five Jantar Mantars (Delhi, Jaipur, Ujjain, Varanasi, Mathura).

question_en: India Gate in New Delhi commemorates soldiers of the British Indian Army who died in:

options.en: Second World War and Burma Campaign
First World War and the Third Anglo-Afghan War

explanation_en: Designed by Lutyens, the memorial has 13,300 names inscribed from 1914-21; the National War Memorial nearby honours post-Independence martyrs.

question_en: Delhi was designated the 'National Capital Territory' with a Legislative Assembly through which Constitutional Amendment?
explanation_en: The 69th Amendment inserted Article 239AA; the Assembly has 70 seats.

question_en: How many seats in the Lok Sabha are allotted to the National Capital Territory of Delhi?
explanation_en: Delhi sends 7 members to the Lok Sabha and 3 to the Rajya Sabha.

question_en: After the unification of the three municipal corporations in May 2022, the Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) has how many wards?
explanation_en: The earlier three corporations had 272 wards in total; delimitation fixed the unified MCD at 250 wards.

question_en: The Delhi High Court was established in the year:
explanation_en: It was set up on 31 October 1966 with the Delhi High Court Act, 1966; earlier Delhi came under the Punjab High Court.

question_en: The Delhi Subordinate Services Selection Board (DSSSB) was constituted in:
explanation_en: DSSSB was set up by the Government of NCT of Delhi in 1996 to recruit for Group B and C posts of Delhi departments and bodies.

question_en: Who is the longest-serving Chief Minister of Delhi?
explanation_en: Sheila Dikshit held office for three consecutive terms from December 1998 to December 2013, about 15 years.

question_en: The first section of the Delhi Metro (Shahdara-Tis Hazari) started operations in:
explanation_en: The Red Line section opened on 24 December 2002; DMRC was incorporated in 1995 with E. Sreedharan as managing director.

question_en: Recognised private schools in Delhi are regulated under which Act?
explanation_en: The Delhi School Education Act and Rules, 1973 regulate recognition, fees and staff service conditions in Delhi schools through the Directorate of Education.

question_en: World Environment Day is observed every year on:
explanation_en: Started by the UN in 1974 following the Stockholm Conference of 1972; Earth Day is on 22 April.

question_en: National Science Day in India is celebrated on 28 February to mark the discovery of:
explanation_en: C. V. Raman announced the Raman Effect (scattering of light) on 28 February 1928 and won the 1930 Nobel Prize in Physics.

question_en: World Teachers' Day is observed internationally on:
explanation_en: UNESCO observes 5 October; India celebrates Teachers' Day on 5 September, the birthday of Dr S. Radhakrishnan.

question_en: National Education Day in India is celebrated on 11 November, the birth anniversary of:
explanation_en: Azad was independent India's first Education Minister; the day has been observed since 2008.

question_en: The International Day of Yoga is observed every year on:
explanation_en: The UN General Assembly proclaimed it in December 2014 on India's proposal; first celebrated in 2015.

question_en: International Literacy Day is observed on:
explanation_en: UNESCO proclaimed it in 1965; first celebrated in 1966. 24 January is National Girl Child Day.

question_en: National Youth Day in India is observed on 12 January, the birth anniversary of:

options.en: Dr A. P. J. Abdul Kalam

explanation_en: The Government of India declared it National Youth Day in 1984, and it has been celebrated from 1985.

question_en: Human Rights Day is observed worldwide on:
explanation_en: It marks the adoption of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights by the UN General Assembly on 10 December 1948.

question_en: Who was the first woman President of India?
explanation_en: Pratibha Patil served from 2007 to 2012; Droupadi Murmu (2022) is the second woman President.

question_en: Who was the first Indian to travel into space (1984), aboard the Soviet Soyuz T-11?
explanation_en: Wing Commander Rakesh Sharma spent about eight days in orbit in April 1984 as part of an Indo-Soviet mission.

question_en: In 2025, who became the first Indian astronaut to visit the International Space Station, on the Axiom-4 mission?
explanation_en: Group Captain Shubhanshu Shukla flew as pilot of Axiom-4 and spent about 18 days on the ISS in June-July 2025.

question_en: Who was the first Indian woman to reach the summit of Mount Everest (1984)?
explanation_en: Bachendri Pal climbed Everest on 23 May 1984; Santosh Yadav later became the first woman to climb it twice.

question_en: Who was the first Indian to win a Nobel Prize?
explanation_en: Tagore won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1913 for Gitanjali; Raman was the first Indian to win in a science field (1930).

question_en: India's first national park, established in 1936 as Hailey National Park, is now called:
explanation_en: Located in Uttarakhand, it was renamed Jim Corbett National Park in 1957; Project Tiger was launched here in 1973.

question_en: India's first satellite, launched in 1975, was named:
explanation_en: Aryabhata, named after the ancient mathematician, was launched on 19 April 1975 from the Soviet Union.

question_en: Who was the first woman judge of the Supreme Court of India (appointed 1989)?
explanation_en: Justice Fathima Beevi joined the Supreme Court in 1989; Leila Seth was the first woman Chief Justice of a High Court (Himachal Pradesh).

question_en: Who was the first Chief Election Commissioner of India?
explanation_en: Sukumar Sen (1950-58) conducted the first general elections of 1951-52.

question_en: Who was the first woman to be awarded the Bharat Ratna?
explanation_en: Indira Gandhi received it in 1971; Mother Teresa (1980), M. S. Subbulakshmi (1998) and Lata Mangeshkar (2001) came later.
